rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods and Results sections report the authors' own laboratory experiments with a scaled-down media filter, two recycled-glass media, three filtration cycles each, measuring retained solids per layer and OCT fouling coverage (Tables 2, 3, 5; Figs 5, 6).
rows.notes: The study is a laboratory methodological study assessing the feasibility of optical coherence tomography to quantify particle fouling across the depth of a pressurised media filter used with reclaimed wastewater. It contains no crop, yield, crop-type or environmental-condition data and reports nothing on the effectiveness of drip irrigation for crop production. The claim that drip irrigation effectiveness varies with crop type and environmental conditions is not supported by any result in this study; the citation is a misattribution. Not a precondition of the claimed effect, so upstream is false; the technology (media filtration for drip systems) is a component of drip irrigation but the effect claimed (crop yield response) is entirely absent.

notes: Full text appears complete apart from references and figure/table bodies. The study concerns filter fouling measurement methodology (OCT vs gravimetric TSS) and has no bearing on crop yield effects of drip irrigation.
